before_times: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: a hearing test, a free screening, a hearing aid check or repair, or earwax removal (the clinic's own visit types; never symptoms typed into the AI)
do you wear hearing aids now
a health plan (its name only), or paying yourself
the best way to reach you: texts, email, or a relay or captioned call
after_time: would you like to bring someone whose voice you know (it helps with part of the test)
anything the clinic should know to help, like a wheelchair, or an interpreter for spoken or sign language
for a care home visit: the place's name, the room, and who meets the audiologist
secure_page_only: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the card
a doctor's order, where the plan asks for one: the doctor's name only, and the clinic gets the order itself
health history: ear infections or surgery, medicines, noise at work, and when the hearing changed
current hearing aids (the maker and model), and the last hearing test date
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18, or the consent of the person who decides for an adult who can't
intake_questions.never_asked: Rosie never asks for symptoms, results or medicines in the AI chat; what a patient types anyway is checked for danger, and the details go only to the secure page
intake_questions.who_may_book: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to this care (a switch)

stop.words: hearing that dropped suddenly, in one or both ears, over a few days or less (with or without new ringing or fullness)
stop.say: Sudden hearing loss needs a doctor today. Please see your own doctor, an urgent care or an emergency room today. Don't wait for a hearing test.
stop.booking: no booking in that conversation; if it comes in before a booked visit, the visit stays booked, the same words are sent, and the owner is told with initials only

stop.words: ear pain with fluid, pus or blood coming from the ear, or ear pain with a high fever
stop.say: This needs a doctor today. Please see your own doctor or an urgent care today, before any hearing test.

stop.words: dizziness or spinning that started suddenly, or ringing in one ear that started suddenly
stop.say: This needs a doctor today. Please see your own doctor or an urgent care today, before any hearing test.

stop.words: a face that droops, weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or a hard blow to the head

go_on.words: an ear that feels blocked or full, with no pain
go_on.what: one safety question first: did the hearing drop suddenly, is fluid coming from the ear, or is there dizziness? Any yes: the 'see a doctor today' words and no booking; all no: the booking goes on

go_on.words: hearing that has slowly gotten worse, muffled voices, trouble on the phone, or a hearing aid that stopped working
go_on.what: matched to the clinic's own visit types; Rosie never judges how serious it is, and same-day times need the owner's OK

safety_and_stop_words.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988; the danger words are checked in every message, every time

steps.name: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before the visit (a same-day visit: before the time is held); one reminder before it's due
steps.who: every new patient; returning patients once a year, or when their health changes
steps.result: not done by its due date: Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the desk or the door, before the test), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered; some services only (hearing aids are often not covered); not covered; or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the patient may cancel free)

steps.name: A doctor's order, where the plan asks for one
steps.when: before the visit, or before the plan is billed
steps.who: a patient whose plan pays for the test only with a doctor's order
steps.result: the clinic asks the doctor's office for it itself: a to-do for the front desk with its due date; the patient is never asked to fetch it

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients
steps.when: told while booking; given in the time the rules set (the example clinic: within 1 business day)
steps.who: every patient paying for themselves, and hearing aids a plan doesn't pay for
steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

steps.name: A doctor's OK before hearing aids, where the rules require one
steps.who: a child, or anyone the state's rules name (a switch); anyone with the warning signs found at the ear check
steps.result: the aids wait until it's on file; the test itself can go on

steps.name: The care home's OK
steps.who: the host place agrees to host the visits
steps.result: no OK: no times at that place

first_steps_and_forms.prep: bring a photo ID, the plan card and any hearing aids you wear now, and someone whose voice you know if you like; stay away from loud noise and earbuds the day of the test; at a care home: the medicine list ready with the nurse, and a quiet room

staff.skills: audiologists: full hearing tests, children's tests, earwax removal, fittings, adjustments, repairs and results; hearing aid specialists: fittings, adjustments, cleanings and repairs, and the tests the state's rules let them run to fit aids (a switch); only people cleared for visits away go to care homes and homes
staff.licenses_or_certificates: each audiologist's own license, per state; each hearing aid specialist's own license or registration, per state
staff.supervision: who may test or fit whom comes from the state form (a switch); in the example clinic, a first full test and every child's test are with an audiologist; a hearing aid specialist is never booked for work beyond their license
staff.who_oks: the owner OKs same-day visits and home visits, and anything a hearing aid specialist flags
staff.stand_in: an audiologist out: another audiologist takes the test (Sam is one), or new times; a hearing aid specialist out: an audiologist does the fitting or the check, or new times; a hearing aid specialist never stands in for a test beyond their license

children_and_age.who_may_book: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to this care (a switch)
children_and_age.minors_texts: a minor's texts go to the parent or guardian; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
children_and_age.minors_rules: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)

visit.check_in: at the clinic: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or home: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or family member named on the booking
visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; test results, notes and hearing aid settings stay in the clinic's own records, never in Rosie or a text

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: always: each audiologist holds their own active license from the state's board; anyone who fits and sells prescription hearing aids holds the state's hearing aid license or registration (a switch from the state form)
license.who: each person: audiologists, and hearing aid specialists (also called dispensers or fitters); the practice too where the state's form registers hearing aid sellers or their places
license.ask: each person's license number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it); the practice's registration from the owner, where the state asks
license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it

never_in_a_text: texts carry only the clinic's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, results or medicines; at the clinic, not the audiologist's name either; when the audiologist or hearing aid specialist comes to a care home or home, their name stays, for the door check; a READY text says only that the order is in
languages: English and Spanish; a spoken or sign language interpreter is set up by the clinic when asked
